items.title: Fans Are 'Disappointed' Over Mariah Carey's 'Depressing' Gucci Holiday Campaign & 'Boring' Styling
items.summary: Report on fan backlash to Gucci's Mariah Carey holiday campaign (directed by Harmony Korine, set to 'All I Want for Christmas Is You'), with quoted social posts calling the ad cold, emotionless and dated; one commenter compared the luxury styling to 'if JCPenney was trying to be luxury.' Direct critical consumer-reaction coverage, not brand-supplied material; still being actively discussed this week per item 005 below.

items.source: X (Gucci official account repost + search aggregation)
items.title: GUCCI GIFT campaign post with Mariah Carey
items.summary: Gucci's official X post promoting the 'Gucci Gift' holiday film with Mariah Carey, directed by Harmony Korine. Brand-owned activation post; included for completeness of channel mix since it is the anchor post that drove the subsequent fan-reaction wave (items 001, 005). Page was paywalled/blocked for live metrics, so engagement fields are null.

items.title: Gucci Discount Strategy Puts Pressure On Luxury Rivals; Louis Vuitton Isn't Following
items.summary: Forbes analysis of Gucci's unusual move to cut prices on flagship handbags and sneakers (e.g. the Padlock Crystal Top Handle cut ~30%, from EUR3,500 to EUR2,450) after 13 consecutive quarters of falling sales; frames this as breaking a luxury pricing taboo that competitors like Louis Vuitton are resisting, with no sustained sales recovery yet despite the cuts (Q3 2026 revenue still down 6% comparable).

items.title: Gucci Gift with Mariah Carey - official film, viewer comment backlash
items.summary: Official Gucci holiday film upload drew critical viewer comments comparing the tone to horror content ('episode of AHS', 'vampire party vibes') and describing it as 'sterile, cold, and devoid of humanity' despite the nostalgic source song; genuine organic viewer sentiment distinct from the brand's intended festive framing. View/like/comment counts not retrievable via available tooling, engagement fields null.

items.title: Is Gucci Still Worth Buying in 2026?
items.summary: Consumer-facing value/resale guide reporting the Gucci GG Marmont's average resale price fell from about $1,600 to $853 amid market oversupply, while noting pre-owned Gucci commonly trades 30-50% below retail across authenticated platforms and most pieces depreciate 30-45% immediately after purchase; frames Gucci resale as liquid but not appreciating versus top-tier peers. Independent consumer-economics critique, not brand-supplied.

items.title: Demna's Fashion Show Premier (PurseForum thread)
items.summary: Active PurseForum thread where handbag-collector members react to Demna's runway output for Gucci; page could not be fully fetched (403) so detailed member quotes are not available, but thread remains open and recently active discussing the designer's direction, consistent with other forum threads showing mixed-to-skeptical sentiment on construction and styling choices. Listed with limited detail rather than fabricated content.

items.title: "Is Gucci on boycott list" / "Why is Gucci so tacky" TikTok discover topics
items.summary: TikTok discover-page topic clusters show active creator content questioning whether Gucci belongs on a boycott list and mocking the brand as tacky/overrated, reflecting a persistent strand of Gen-Z sentiment that the logo-driven aesthetic has lost cultural cachet since peak 2020-2022 virality. Genuine organic platform signal; individual video engagement counts not retrievable via available tooling so numeric fields are null.

items.title: Kering slides as Gucci sales fall 6% despite in-line Q3 revenue
items.summary: Earnings-desk coverage confirming Gucci Q3 2026 sales fell 6% comparable, with North America's growth decelerating sharply to +1% in Q3 after +9% to +10% gains in Q1/Q2, even as conversion and average ticket improved; China traffic remains the biggest drag per Kering's CFO. Useful region-specific data point showing NA momentum cooling, not just a China story.

notes: Dedup vs 2026-11-22 NA pool: that pool already covered the Lyst Q3 ranking, the two PurseForum Flora/quality threads, the whyyoushouldcare/fashionchitchat Substack pieces, the Switzerland watch-division layoffs, and two Pre-Fall/FW26 YouTube creator reviews. Today's pool deliberately surfaces NEW items/angles: the Mariah Carey 'Gucci Gift' campaign backlash (news + official X post + YouTube comment reaction, a fresh news cycle from early-to-mid November still being discussed), the Goldman Sachs Q4 forecast cut (new analyst data point), the Forbes price-cut piece (distinct from yesterday's TheIndustry.fashion item, different numbers/angle), a resale-value guide with specific GG Marmont depreciation figures, a new PurseForum thread (Demna's Fashion Show Premier, distinct from the Flora/quality-issue threads already pooled), a TikTok boycott/overrated discover-topic cluster (new SNS source), region-specific NA growth deceleration data from Q3 earnings coverage, and the WWD business-units restructuring story (new structural/operational angle).

Freshness: items span 2026-11-02 (Mariah Carey campaign launch, still generating fresh commentary cycles through this week) to 2026-11-21 (Goldman Sachs forecast cut); all within the 14-day hard cap and the majority within 7 days.

Channel mix: 5 news, 2 sns (X official post, YouTube comment reaction) +1 sns (TikTok discover topic) = 3 sns total, 2 community (designersignals.com resale guide, PurseForum thread). This meets the >=3 sns/community target (5 total). True Instagram/Facebook native posts and Reddit searches ran dry today despite repeated site-scoped and keyword queries in English; the PurseForum 'Demna's Fashion Show Premier' thread returned HTTP 403 on fetch so it is pooled with limited detail rather than fabricated member quotes.

Priority-A source check: per buzz_registry.json, Facebook (I=4.2) is NA's only Priority-A sns/community source; site-scoped and keyword searches for Gucci-related Facebook content ran dry (Facebook's public search surface does not expose post-level results to web search) - flagged as dry rather than padded.

Critical-angle searches were productive: price-cut/discount-strategy framing (items 003, 004), resale-value depreciation data (item 006), the Mariah Carey campaign backlash across three sub-angles (items 001, 002, 005), and boycott/overrated TikTok sentiment (item 008) all surfaced genuine independent or data-driven criticism, not activation coverage. A dedicated Reddit search (r/handbags, r/luxury) ran dry today despite multiple query variants.

Balance: of 10 items, 5 are critical/skeptical or hard-negative-data (001 campaign backlash, 003 analyst downgrade, 004 price-cut-as-distress-signal, 006 resale depreciation, 008 boycott/overrated sentiment), 1 is the brand's own activation post included for completeness (002), 1 is organic negative viewer reaction to that activation (005), and the remainder (007, 009, 010) are descriptive/structural. This is not a positive-skewed pool.

Cross-region note: the Gucci Harrods/Demna retail-concept story was found but excluded from this NA pool as EU-origin (UK market, Paris-concept rollout); flagging in case EU's collector has not already pooled it.
